description: Alternative estimators of the realized_cer -> drift log-odds slope under different dependence assumptions, to show the slope is stable across dependence structures (only 7 models, so a model-clustered SE is not credible). All estimators fit realized_cer ONLY (plus intercept) for mutual comparability.

reference_slopes.note: The 4.79 headline is the ADJUSTED message-clustered logit slope (adjusts n_errors, char_len, corrupted_negation, corrupted_numeral, C(family)). The dependence estimators here are UNIVARIATE, so their natural reference is the univariate message-clustered anchor (8.79). The univariate slope is ~2x the adjusted slope because, unadjusted, realized_cer absorbs the drift-increasing effect of correlated corruption covariates (notably corrupted_numeral and n_errors). That gap is ADJUSTMENT, not dependence; the B9 question is only about dependence.

per_model_pooled_dl.label: Per-model message-clustered cluster-robust logit (drift ~ realized_cer), pooled across models by DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis (preferred model-level estimator; 7 models is too few for a model-clustered SE)

gee.label: GEE population-averaged logit (drift ~ realized_cer; Binomial family, independence fallback working correlation, groups=message_id, robust sandwich SE)
gee.notes: FALLBACK: exchangeable working correlation returned non-finite parameters (correlation ran away) on this cohort (large ~700-row message clusters with strong within-message drift correlation); reverted to an independence working correlation with the same robust sandwich SE, which yields a consistent slope and a valid cluster-robust SE regardless of the true correlation.

bootstrap_message.label: Nonparametric cluster bootstrap of drift ~ realized_cer, resampling message-level clusters (762) with replacement, 500 resamples

bootstrap_model.label: Nonparametric cluster bootstrap of drift ~ realized_cer, resampling model-level clusters (7) with replacement, 500 resamples -- UNSTABLE: too few clusters for a trustworthy cluster bootstrap; CI is wide/erratic and reported for honesty, not relied upon (see per_model_pooled_slope for the preferred model-level estimator)

conclusion.summary: The realized_cer log-odds slope is STABLE across dependence assumptions: all four estimators lie in 8.79-9.23 (spread 0.44, <= 5.0% from the univariate anchor 8.79). The preferred model-level estimator is the DerSimonian-Laird per-model pool (7 models is too few for a model-clustered SE); it shows large between-model heterogeneity (tau^2=2.66, I^2=99%) but every model's slope is large and positive (range 6.5-10.6). The model-level cluster bootstrap is reported honestly as UNSTABLE (7 clusters: much wider CI than the message-level bootstrap). The exchangeable GEE diverged on this cohort and fell back to an independence working correlation (see its notes). None of these dependence estimators diverges materially from the others.
